transcript.label: Transcript turn 7 · the case reveal
transcript.said: Beds it is — and what you’ve described lines up closely with a hospital we worked with. Let me show you their day rather than describe it. One thing to watch as you read it: that bed stopped earning hours before it was empty. Does that look like your day? And is there anything about your own setup you’d add to what’s there?
transcript.note: The user’s line is paraphrased in the transcript (“commits to the bed problem”).

sample.name: Four stops, one bed
sample.what: The library’s chain, as the approved transcript drew it: four boxes, the last one red. Each box carries the bed mark and whether anything is billing. Tap a box for its sheet and Add yours.

text: Beds it is. What you’ve described lines up closely with a hospital we worked with.
Let me show you their day rather than describe it. One thing to watch: that bed stopped earning hours before it was empty.
Does that look like your day? If yours is different anywhere, add it on the drawing and it comes into your message.
chat.note: The bed stops earning long before it is empty.
prompts: Yes, that looks like our day

blocks.title: The bed that stopped earning
blocks.deck: One bed through one day. Watch where the bill stops, and how long it stays stopped.

blocks.label: One bed, one day
blocks.caption: Nothing bills on this bed across this whole stretch. That includes pharmacy, tests, scans and procedures.

sheets.title: Final bill closed
sheets.text: The leaving patient’s final bill is closed and sent for insurance approval. From here nothing more is charged to this bed.
sheets.entry: When does the final bill close at your hospital?
sheets.entry_hint: For example: nearer 1 PM, after the pharmacy check

sheets.title: Approval, payment, family briefing
sheets.text: The insurer approves, the family pays and is told what happens at home. All this time the patient is still in the bed.
sheets.entry_hint: For example: approval takes 3 hours for some insurers

sheets.title: Patient leaves, bed made ready
sheets.text: The patient finally leaves. Housekeeping cleans the bed and gets it ready for the next patient.
sheets.entry: Who readies the bed, and how long does it take?

sheets.title: Next patient admitted
sheets.text: The next patient is admitted. Only now does a new bill open against this bed, and the bed starts earning again.
sheets.entry: When does your next patient usually reach the bed?
sheets.entry_hint: For example: around 5 PM, later on busy days

ask_more.label: Anything about your own setup you’d add?
ask_more.hint: For example: our ICU works differently

blocks.label: Dead bed time
blocks.value: Last bill closed to next bill opened
blocks.sub: Often half a day or more on one bed. Most hospitals have never measured it on its own.

review.note: Kept as a variation: the chain with the Bed Management layer.
